articles.headline: Bible Presentation at Lombard St. Central Presbyterian Church
articles.author: Veritas
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Having obtained a ticket of admittance to a Bible presentation at Lombard Street Central Church, on Thursday evening last, in spite of the heavy rain I went thither about eight o'clock, where I found assembled about two hundred persons. The exercises commenced with a fervent prayer offered to the throne of grace by Rev. Mr. Mallory [VERIFY], after which the Bible, in behalf of the congregation, was presented by Mr. Robert Jones (senior elder of the church) ... received by their pastor, Rev. J. B. Reeve. (Also named, reading uncertain: Galtor [VERIFY] (in charge of the choir (Mr.)); A. Colly [VERIFY] (superintendent of the singing school (Mr.)).)
people: pastor, Lombard Street Central Presbyterian Church, recipient of the Bible (Rev.; inscription reads 'Rev. John B. Reeve')
senior elder of the church; presented the Bible

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Susan Onely)
articles.author: John E. Onely
articles.summary: Can any one inform me of the whereabouts of Miss Susan Onely, who came from Virginia, in the year 1847, to the City of Philadelphia, Pa., and was raised principally by a Quaker family by the name of Willetts, who reside on the corner of 8th [VERIFY: 5th or 8th] and Callowhill Sts., Phila. The last account we heard of her, was, that she had gone somewhere in the State to live.
people: sought; came from Virginia to Philadelphia in 1847, raised by the Willetts family, 8th [VERIFY] and Callowhill Sts.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Rebecca Dowden)
articles.author: Mary Dowden
articles.summary: Can any person inform me of the whereabouts of Miss Rebecca Dowden, of Philadelphia, formerly of Baltimore, Md.? She has been residing in Philadelphia. Her sister-in-law Mrs. Elizabeth Field, died in Woodstown, N. J., about three years ago. Her daughter, Harriet Dowden, is deceased. The estate of the parties is to be settled.
people: sought; of Philadelphia, formerly of Baltimore

articles.summary: Acknowledgments: Carlisle Sabbath School, Pa., 10.00; Mrs. Lydia W. Price, of Attleborough, Penna., 2.25; ... Of W. S. Walker, for papers sold, Frankford, Pa., 1.25; Mrs. M. Cheen [VERIFY], Frankford, Pa., 2.25; ... Sarah Coque, Princeton, N.J., Sarah Beahman, both per Rev. T. Gould, ...
people: paid for papers sold, Frankford, Pa.

articles.headline: Correction (Bethel Church collection)
articles.summary: The true amount collected in Bethel Church was not $7,000 as incorrectly stated in our last week's issue. This is a mistake. The correct amount taken in (by class leaders and all) was $727.85.

articles.headline: Fairs (Bethel, Little Wesley, Big Wesley, St. Thomas', Masonic Hall)
articles.summary: There are Fairs holding at Bethel Church, at Little Wesley, at Big Wesley, at St. Thomas' and at the Masonic Hall. Bethel church on Christmas Eve, was so crowded that it was almost impossible for a person to make his way from one side of the house to the other.

articles.headline: Masonic Sermon (Union A.M.E. Church)
articles.summary: On last Sabbath afternoon the Order of Masons assembled in the Union A.M.E. Church to hear a discourse then to be delivered by the Rev. Anthony L. Stanford, having been selected by them for that occasion. His text was: 'I am doing a great work, and cannot come down.'

articles.headline: Soldiers' Fair (Ladies' Union Association, Sansom Street Hall)
articles.summary: The Fair of the Ladies' Union Association takes place at Sansom Street Hall, commencing on Tuesday, the 5th inst. (continuing on through the 6th and 7th insts.). Season tickets, 25 cts. This is a very proper move.

articles.headline: Married (Cook and Appoe, St. Thomas')
articles.summary: At St. Thomas', on last Tuesday, at ten minutes past five o'clock, A.M., Mr. John F. Cook, of Washington, to Miss E. Appoe [VERIFY], of Philadelphia. They were married, and left for Washington at midnight.

articles.headline: Appointment (free-will offerings at Union A.M.E. and Bethel for the paper and Book Concern)
articles.summary: On next Sabbath, by Divine permission, we shall preach in Union A.M.E. church, at half-past 7 o'clock, at which time we are to have a free will offering for the benefit of the paper and Book Concern. ... The Rev. A. L. Stanford, the much respected minister in charge, has kindly volunteered to set apart that evening. On the third Sabbath of this month, at three o'clock, Elder Schureman has kindly devoted his church to our especial benefit.

articles.headline: Frederick Douglass Lyceum, election of officers
articles.author: J. J. Minton
articles.summary: At a meeting of the Frederick Douglass Lyceum, held on the 9th of December, the following officers were elected for the ensuing three months. ... Mr. Editor: Will you oblige the Frederick Douglass Lyceum by inserting the above in the columns of your most noble paper? Philadelphia, Dec. 28th, 1863. (Also named, reading uncertain: J. B. Ballard [VERIFY] (vice president).)

articles.author: Joshua Woodlin
articles.summary: At an annual communication of the R. W. G. Lodge of A. Y. M., of the State of New Jersey, held in the city of Burlington, Dec. 28th, 1863, A. L. 5863, the following Brothers, who had been previously elected, were duly installed to their respective offices. (Also named, reading uncertain: Henry Mackey [VERIFY] (R. W. Grand Master).)

District Deputy G. M., Middlesex and Essex

articles.summary: The accumulating interests which are clustering around our race, amid the revolutions in this country, have prompted the African Civilization Society to a more vigorous prosecution of its designs ... Constitution of the African Civilization Society. Preamble. It has pleased Almighty God to permit the interior of Africa to be made known ... (Also named, reading uncertain: J. C. Bustil [VERIFY] (trustee, Philadelphia).)

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting (hall on Lombard Street near Broad)
articles.author: Thomas H. Cooper [VERIFY]
articles.summary: We give notice to the friends and the public generally, that there will be a Quarterly Meeting held on Sunday, Jan. 17th, 1864, in the hall on Lombard Street, near the S. E. corner of Broad. Thomas H. Cooper [VERIFY], Missionary.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (Book Concern receipts)
articles.summary: Acknowledgments: James Thorp, Newark, N. J. ... Miss Mary Davis, Burlington, N. J., last year's balance; Miss Matilda Green, Leiperville, Pa.; ... Aaron Byard, Haddonfield, N. J., 2.00; Thos. Stukely, do. do., 1.00; Rev. Wm. Winder, Freehold, N. J., 1.00; Wm. Whipple, Columbia, Pa., for to send the Recorder to soldiers ...

articles.headline: Disappointment at Union A.M.E. Church
articles.summary: It was published, in our paper, that we would preach in Union Church, on last Sabbath night, and take up a collection, for the benefit of the book concern and paper. But, we are sorry to say, notwithstanding that it was the hour agreed upon by Elder Stanford and myself, at a late hour on Saturday night, he informed me, that the trustees objected, for two very unjustifiable reasons, which we will not mention, but we would like to know who has charge of the pulpit, the elder in charge or the trustees? Elder Schureman has set apart the 3d Sabbath in this month, at 3 o'clock, P.M.

articles.headline: Letter from a soldier of the 3d Colored Regiment (box from a young lady)
articles.summary: A very interesting letter was shown to us a day or two ago, from one of the soldiers of the 3d Colored Regiment of the U.S., on Morris' Island, S. C. It was in relation to a box of cakes, preserves, pickles, candies, tooth brushes, tobacco, &c., by one of our good and generous young ladies. ... By her request we keep the name concealed.

articles.headline: Philadelphia Herald (new paper)
articles.summary: This is the name of a new paper in our city. We have received Vol. 1, Nos. 1 & 2, for 1864. It is a medium size, and is to be devoted to the interests of our people. It is published every Saturday, at No. 448 [VERIFY] N. Third St., Philadelphia, at $2 per annum, by Mr. Parker T. Smith, who was formerly connected with the Anglo-African.
people: publisher, Philadelphia Herald, No. 448 [VERIFY] N. Third St.; formerly of the Anglo-African

articles.headline: Fair at Sansom St. Hall (closed)
articles.summary: The Ladies' Fair, for the benefit of the soldiers, closed last Thursday night. They were well patronized, and hope they done well.

articles.headline: Grand Lodge of Pennsylvania (Prince Hall), election and installation of officers
articles.author: A. P. Faucett
articles.summary: Philadelphia, Dec. 28, 1863, A. L. 5863. At the Fourth Quarterly Communication of the R. W. G. Lodge for the State of Pennsylvania, held at their Hall, South Eleventh, below Pine Street, on the 7th day of December, the following brethren were elected to their respective positions, and on the 28th of December, being St. John the Evangelist's Day, were duly installed.

committee on landmarks (also printed 'R. H. Gleaves', by-laws and correspondence)

articles.headline: Married (Moston and Tilghman)
articles.summary: On the 4th inst., by the Rev. W. D. W. Schureman, Mr. Jas. E. Moston [VERIFY], of Philadelphia, to Miss Henrietta Tilghman, of Baltimore, Md. (Other marriages in the column: Ohio, Indiana, and Freehold, N.J., by Rev. W. H. W. Winder: Mr. Charles Williams to Miss Margaret Ann Henderson.)

articles.headline: Died (Cassella Peterson Craig)
articles.summary: Suddenly, in Woodbury, N. J., Dec. 23, in the triumph of faith, Cassella [VERIFY] Peterson Craig, wife of Thomas Craig, and daughter of Mary Trusty [VERIFY] and the late Rev. D. H. Peterson. 'She is not dead but sleepeth.' Her remains were interred in Johnson's Cemetery, Camden, on Sabbath, Dec. 27th. (Also named, reading uncertain: Cassella Peterson Craig [VERIFY] (deceased, Woodbury, N.J.; wife of Thomas Craig).)

articles.headline: The Report of the Bethel Church
articles.author: W. D. W. Schureman
articles.summary: Mr. Editor, Dear Sir: This will inform you and the public, that Bethel A. M. E. Church, S. Sixth Street, Philadelphia, Pa., has been repaired and renovated, at a cost of sixteen hundred dollars ($1600) instead of thirteen hundred ($1300) as before published, owing to recent improvements in addition to the original. The collection realized, a few Sabbaths ago, $727.85, in connection with the result of a fair that was held in said church during the holidays, of which was cleared $755.81, with $200 that was collected by Rev. S. Smith, for said purpose, has liquidated the entire debt.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting: Our West Section Mission (hall on Lombard Street near Broad)
articles.author: Thomas H. Cooper
articles.summary: There will be a quarterly meeting held on Sunday, January 17th inst., in the Hall, on Lombard Street, near the S. E. corner of Broad. This will be our first quarterly meeting held in this section. We therefore hope to see a large number on the occasion. Come, friends, and encourage us in endeavoring to establish ourselves in this section of the city. Thomas H. Cooper, City Missionary.

articles.headline: Holidays Are Over (church fairs)
articles.summary: The fairs and the great bustle are over. Bethel Church, St. Thomas', Little Pine Street Baptist, Big Wesley, Little Wesley, and the Masonics are all over. Bethel Church has done nobly. They have cleared over seven hundred and fifty dollars, aside from one hundred dollars for Wilberforce University. We refer our readers to the Rev. William D. W. Schureman's letter.

articles.headline: Religious Services (Bethel collection for the Book Concern)
articles.summary: We hope that Bethel Church will be crowded on Sabbath afternoon, at 3 o'clock. We shall look for all true friends of the church, Book Concern and paper, as there will be a collection taken up to aid us in carrying on the work ... It has been two years since we have asked Bethel Church for aid ... She has been renovated anew, at an expense of about $1600, and has paid, we believe, the last cent, within two months.

articles.headline: A Visit to Washington and Baltimore (Dr. J. H. Brown's lectures)
articles.summary: Dr. J. H. Brown, of Philadelphia, has, we understand, made arrangements to lecture in the cities of Baltimore and Washington. We do, beyond a doubt, consider Dr. Brown an excellent lecturer of his profession, and he can also hold an audience spell-bound.

articles.headline: Steam Dyeing, Scouring and Repairing Works (editorial puff for Jas. W. Brown)
articles.summary: We call special attention to the advertisement of our very highly and esteemed friend, Mr. Jas. W. Brown, No. 136 [VERIFY] South Sixth Street. Mr. Brown is not only professor of scouring, cleaning and making gentlemen's clothes look new, but mends them in such a way, as can hardly be seen ... Give Mr. Brown a trial and judge for yourselves, at No. 136 [VERIFY] South Sixth Street, Philadelphia.
people: steam dyer and scourer, No. 136 [VERIFY] South Sixth Street

articles.headline: An Important Request (A. L. Stanford on 'Disappointment at Union A.M.E. Church') and Weaver's Answer
articles.author: A. L. Stanford
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Please permit me here to state in this the 3d number of Vol. IV, of the Christian Recorder, that I find an article in the preceding number of said paper, entitled: 'Disappointment at Union A. M. E. Church.' The import of this article I claim has to its numerous readers misrepresented said church, trustees thereof and your servant, who is now being honored with the privilege of being the humble pastor. ... N.B. Quarterly meeting at the Union A. M. E. Church, on next Sunday, the 17th inst. [Answer by the editor follows.]

articles.headline: Oysters and Confectioneries (Mr. and Mrs. Gleaves)
articles.summary: We call the special attention of our friends to Mr. and Mrs. Gleaves. We highly recommend to all who want good oysters, to give Mrs. Gleaves a call. She has good accommodations. Walk in, ladies and gentlemen, and get a good dish of oysters, also cakes, candies, and anything in their line, at No. 633 Pine Street.
people: oysters and confectioneries, No. 633 Pine Street (printed 'Mrs. Gleaves')

articles.headline: Letter from Miss Dix (appeal for colored nurses)
articles.author: D. L. Dix
articles.summary: Copy of a letter from Miss Dix to Mrs. Hunn, 26 N. W. Penn Square (Munich St.). Washington, Jan. 6th, 1864. Mrs. Hunn: I am asked for nurses for the colored soldiers at Camp Stanton, Md. Col. Birney writes that he wants those who can be trusted to give stimulants and medicines ... [Editor:] Shall the appeal be answered by the many noble-hearted colored women of this city?

articles.headline: Shiloh Baptist Church: Rev. Jeremiah Asher appointed chaplain of the 6th U.S.C.T.; resolutions
articles.summary: To all whom it may concern. The Rev. Jeremiah Asher, nearly fifteen years pastor of the Shiloh Baptist Church, has been appointed chaplain to the 6th Regiment of U. S. C. T. The church have granted him leave of absence, and he has joined the regiment. Correspondents will please take notice, and direct as follows: 6th U. S. C. T., Camp near Yorktown, Va. (Also named, reading uncertain: Westward F. Keeling [VERIFY] (deacon, Shiloh Baptist Church); John S. Kinney [VERIFY] (deacon, Shiloh Baptist Church); Peter Quinn [VERIFY] (deacon, Shiloh Baptist Church); James M. Auter [VERIFY] (trustee, Shiloh Baptist Church).)

articles.headline: Frankford, Twenty-third Ward: enlistment of colored soldiers and meeting at the A.M.E. Church
articles.author: Jacob Trusty; Peter R. Blake [VERIFY]; Randall Pleasant [VERIFY], committee
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: We thought we would let you and your many readers know what is going on in the Twenty-third Ward, Frankford, Pa. The call for colored soldiers reached us, and the young men have responded to the call. Seventeen have enlisted, fifteen in the army and two in the navy. The evening after they enlisted, we called a meeting in the A. M. E. Church at Frankford, to encourage them for their bravery. (Also named, reading uncertain: Elias Cary [VERIFY] (enlisted); Benjamin Woodlin [VERIFY] (enlisted); Albert Farral [VERIFY] (enlisted).)

articles.headline: Collection in Bethel Church
articles.summary: Last Sabbath was the day set apart for us to preach and present the righteous claims of the paper and Book Concern. We are sorry that we were very suddenly taken sick on the Thursday night previous ... The galleries of the church were pretty well crowded ... but we saw but very few class leaders, local preachers and exhorters, and very few of the stewards, and quite a sprinkle of the trustees, and some, we understand, were seen leaving the church before the services commenced ... Mr. Abraham Field, steward in the church and our city carrier principally, made some very interesting remarks ... Elder Schureman made an appeal, and we took up on the occasion $30.73.
people: steward, Bethel Church; city carrier of the Recorder

articles.headline: Colored Public School, Sixth St., Philadelphia (petitions for the franchise; Miss Donelly)
articles.summary: We have been informed from good and reliable sources, that some petitions which were circulated through our city, for signers, to be sent to the United States Congress, were presented at the Colored School, in Sixth St., of which the teachers are all white. Mr. Byrd, we believe, of the boys' department, encouraged the project, but when it was presented to a Miss Donelly, who is the principal of the girls' department, she refused to encourage it ... we can break the school up by preventing our children from going.

articles.headline: Colored Troops (8th U.S.C.T. departs Chelten Hill)
articles.summary: Another brave regiment, the Eighth Regiment United States Colored Troops, took their departure from Chelten Hill on the 16th inst., en route for, some say, Hilton Head, South Carolina, and others say Texas. The men are all well trained ... They crossed over to Jersey from the foot of Walnut Street. The crowd that went down to see them off was immense, both white and colored. They took the cars for New York.

articles.headline: Book Notice: William C. Thurman, 'The Sealed Book of Daniel Opened'
articles.summary: Mr. William C. Thurman is the author of a work called 'The Sealed Book of Daniel Opened.' We have not had the time to give this book a thorough examination ... It is printed upon fine paper and in beautiful type, and has been published by John Goodyear, Esq., corner of Seventeenth [VERIFY] and Pine Streets, Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Dr. Longfellow, Dentistry (puff)
articles.summary: We refer our readers to Dr. Longfellow's advertisement in another column of our paper. We understand that he is kept very busy, so much so that he has had to wait upon many of his patients upon the Sabbath.

articles.headline: Presentation to Mr. Harry Jarvis by the Philadelphia waiters (Willard's Hotel, Washington)
articles.summary: Among the many incidents of the New Year, was the presentation of a magnificent silver goblet, at Willard's Hotel, Washington, by the Philadelphia waiters, to their efficient and gentlemanly head waiter, Mr. Harry Jarvis. The presentation was made by Mr. Robert Morrow, in behalf of himself and his associates ... Professor Nelson Parker then addressed the assembly in an eloquent manner.

articles.headline: Personal: Madam Josephine Ruffin visits the Book Store
articles.summary: Madam Josephine Ruffin, the great Dramatic Reader, from Boston, Massachusetts, was in our book-store last Wednesday to see us. We are sorry that we were called out ... She is en route for Washington on a professional visit.

articles.headline: Getting Ready for the General Conference
articles.summary: Our General Conference and the M. E. General Conference, both meet in this city of Philadelphia, on the first Monday in May; and can't we enter into some sort of an arrangement to have excursion tickets from the West to Pittsburgh, and we will try to make an arrangement from Pittsburgh to Philadelphia?

articles.headline: Notice: A.M.E. City Mission preaching at the Hall, Broad and Lombard
articles.summary: Preaching every Sabbath, will be held at the Hall, one door below the south-east corner of Broad and Lombard Sts., under the charge of the City Missionary of the A. M. E. Church, at 10 1/2 o'clock, A.M., 3 o'clock, P.M. and 7 1/2 o'clock, P.M.; Sabbath School, 9 o'clock, A.M. and 1 1/2 [VERIFY] o'clock, P.M.

Simpson; Recording Secretary, William H. Dorsey [VERIFY]; Corresponding Secretary, Joseph Brister [VERIFY]; Treasurer, William H. Minton [VERIFY]. (Also named, reading uncertain: Joshua B. articles.headline: Obituary: Joseph R. Adger
articles.author: James W. Brown
articles.summary: On January 22d, 1864, after a short illness, Joseph R. Adger, died, in the 19th year of his age. Pen cannot describe the loss which his family and the community sustain ... We find him when the Governor of Pa. called for aid, in July last, during the raid of the rebel hordes upon our soil ... joining with the first colored company formed in our city or State, to march to the defence of the Capitol and State ... he applied for a commission to recruit for our colored regiments ... shipped on board of the U. S. Ship Ticonderoga ... taken sick and carried to his father's on the 18th inst., and on the 22d he died.
people: deceased, aged 19th year; member of the first colored company (July 1863); recruiter; U.S. Ship Ticonderoga

articles.headline: Preachers' Meeting (Philadelphia District)
articles.summary: We call attention to the Preacher's Meeting of the Philadelphia District, and would say that said meeting is again revived, and will meet on every Tuesday, at 10 o'clock, in Bethel Church, (Preacher's study) at which time and place they will discuss subjects pertaining to the General Conference, such as the altering of our title, &c.

articles.headline: Last Sabbath (Bethel quarterly meeting; Little Wesley protracted meeting)
articles.summary: We were at Bethel, and heard our young Brother Berley [VERIFY], in the morning, who gave us a good common sense practical discourse, from 1 Samuel xii. 23. Bethel was pretty well filled, as it was Elder Schureman's Quarterly Meeting ... In the afternoon we went to Wesley Church, of which Joseph Smith is the elder. We heard a very good discourse from Father Murray, a local preacher. This church has been holding a protracted meeting for some two weeks ... Brother Smith granted us the privilege of making a few remarks about our paper, (The Recorder) which he and Brother James Fuller greatly endorsed. After the congregation was dismissed, some seven or eight persons came forward and subscribed. Good for little Wesley.
people: member, Little Wesley; endorsed the Recorder (Brother)

articles.headline: Doing All They Can (agents; Brother Davis, Bethel class leader)
articles.summary: We are glad to see that some of our brethren are doing what they can. Brother Dorrell and Brother Davis, of Galesburgh, Ills., Brother H. M. Johnson, of Coxsackie, Brother Shreeves and Brother H. J. Johnson, of New Bedford, and a few others. Yes, Brother Davis, of Baltimore, Md., one of the class leaders of Bethel Church.

articles.headline: Died (son of Mr. Adger, furniture dealer, South St.)
articles.summary: It will be seen in another part of our paper, that a son of Mr. Adger's has departed this life. Mr. Adger is one of our large furniture dealers, in South St.

articles.headline: William Still elected post sutler at Camp William Penn
articles.summary: Mr. William Still, of this city, has been elected post sutler, at Camp William Penn, and has been appointed the same by the Secretary of War; so we have been informed. And Mr. Ellis Pear, one of our best cake and confectionery dealers of this city, is his partner. We wish them great success in their noble undertaking. Mr. Still is also a stove and coal dealer, in 5th, above Arch St.
people: post sutler, Camp William Penn; stove and coal dealer, 5th above Arch St.
partner in the sutlership; cake and confectionery dealer (printed 'Pear')

articles.headline: The General Conference (Twenty-first, Philadelphia, May 1864)
articles.summary: The Twenty-first General Conference of the African Methodist Episcopal Church will sit in the city of Philadelphia just three months from the first Monday in February ... Some are advocating the propriety of three Bishops more, instead of two more.

articles.headline: The West End Mission (Broad and Lombard)
articles.summary: Preaching will be resumed on Sunday, the 31st inst., at the West End Mission, south-east corner of Broad and Lombard Streets, and will continue, under the supervision of the Mission of the A. M. E. Church, every Sabbath, at 10 1/2 o'clock, A.M., and 7 o'clock, P.M. It is hoped that the friends of church extension in the western section will give it their presence and support.

articles.headline: To the Members of Bethel A.M.E. Church (Brooks v. Campbell)
articles.author: W. D. W. Schureman
articles.summary: The design of this article is to disabuse a part of the public mind on the subject of a case which has recently been decided by the court, in the case of brother H. Brooks and the Rev. J. P. Campbell. The Rev. J. P. Campbell was held for slander, in repeatedly referring to the expulsion of the above-named brother upon a charge of fraud. The court decided that the repeated reference by the elder was not slander, thus leaving the case as decided by the church. Philadelphia, Jan. 25, 1864.
people: plaintiff; former Bethel trustee and acting agent, expelled (printed 'H. Brooks')

articles.headline: The Wilberforce Committee (Philadelphia Annual Conference)
articles.author: Stephen Smith
articles.summary: Appointed by the Philadelphia Annual Conference, to receive pledges made at the last Annual Conference, are hereby notified to meet at No. 921 Lombard St., Philadelphia, on the 4th of February, 1864, at 11 o'clock, on important business. Stephen Smith, Chairman of the Committee.

articles.headline: An Elder Sued for Doing His Duty: Henry Brooks vs. Rev. J. P. Campbell (District Court, Judge Hare)
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: This was an action to recover damages for an alleged slander, uttered by defendant, who was the pastor of the A. M. E. Bethel Church, Sixth Street, Philadelphia. Ex-Judge Parsons, counsel for plaintiff; William S. Pierce, Esq., counsel for defendant. The plaintiff (Brooke) alleged that the Rev. Jabez P. Campbell announced from the pulpit his (plaintiff's) expulsion for fraudulent practices. ... The jury returned into court and reported a verdict for defendant, Rev. J. P. Campbell. Thus ended the suit Friday morning, January 22d, 1864. Mr. Brooke was formerly a Trustee of the A. M. E. Bethel Church, Sixth Street, Philadelphia, from April, 1860, to April, 1863. [Signed J. P. Campbell, Philadelphia, Jan. 22, 1864; to be continued.]
people: plaintiff; Bethel trustee April 1860 to April 1863 and agent (also printed 'Brooke', 'Brooks')

articles.headline: Died (William Carpenter)
articles.summary: In this city, on the morning of the 18th inst., in the 59th year of his age, after a lingering illness, which he bore with Christian fortitude, William Carpenter, member of the First Colored M. P. (Israel) Church.
people: deceased, 59th year; member, First Colored M. P. (Israel) Church

articles.headline: Notice: presentation at the A.M.E. Macedonia Church, South Camden
articles.summary: On the evening of the 22d of January, 1864, a presentation was made by three females of the A. M. E. Macedonia Church, in South Camden, to their pastor, through the preacher's steward, the sum of $30, on his salary, they being thus influenced by an itinerant missionary spirit. They went forth out of said church and collected in behalf of their church the above named sum, as follows: Mrs. Sarah E. Brown, $14.75; Mrs. Rosanna Barnes, 10.00; Mrs. Emily Fisher, 5.25.

collector, A.M.E. Macedonia Church, South Camden (Mrs.)

articles.headline: Our Own Book-Store (catalogue of the Book Depository)
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: Catalogue of Books for Sale at the Book Depository of the A M E Church located at No. 619 Pine St., Philadelphia, Pa. A New Pronouncing Bible ... Theological works, Sabbath School presents ... We hope, that brethren of our connexion and friends will send orders, accompanied with the cash, for such works as they themselves ought to study, also the Sabbath Schools, so that our Depository may have an upward, and not a downward tendency. Signed Elisha Weaver, General Book Steward.

articles.headline: A Humane Appeal (papers for colored soldiers)
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: An appeal to the citizens of Philadelphia and elsewhere, in behalf of our brave colored soldiers of the United States, who have left their homes, their wives, their children ... Colored soldiers have written to the editor to know why it is that they cannot be supplied with our paper, as well as white soldiers are supplied with other papers ... There are more than 6000 colored soldiers in and around Fortress Monroe, Yorktown and Norfolk, besides thousands in the Western departments ... those who may feel like aiding the cause can send to our box 2975, Philadelphia, or to 619 Pine St. Signed Elisha Weaver, Ed. (standing; marked Dec5-3m)

articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: I will, by Divine permission, preach at Montrose, N. J. [as printed], on the 17th of March, at Wilksburg, on the 18th, at Danville, on the 20th, at Reading, on the 21st, at Great Valley, on the 23d, and at Downingtown, on the 24th, and will be in Phila., on the 25th. articles.headline: A Word (to Mrs. Satie Douglass)
articles.summary: We would mention to that most estimable lady, Mrs. Satie Douglass, that most cordially and firmly do we endorse all that you have said, and more. We are fully persuaded that Slavery is dead; or, at least, that its hydra-head is bruised and mangled nigh unto death ... Administer another castigation, Mrs. D., and the monster's downfall will surely be materially hastened.

articles.headline: Revivals (Wesley church)
articles.summary: The Holy Spirit is still dwelling with the good people of Wesley church. Rev. Joseph H. [VERIFY] Smith is the worthy pastor in charge. May God bless them in their good work. The churches generally are getting along very well indeed. (Also named, reading uncertain: Joseph H. Smith [VERIFY] (pastor in charge, Wesley church (Rev.)).)

articles.headline: Encouraging (Friends' schools on Raspberry Street)
articles.summary: We have information that the Schools on Raspberry Street, for colored men and women, under the care of the Friends, are in a flourishing condition. Both Schools are unusually large, there being nearly two hundred present at a time. We do hope that our brethren and sisters will fully appreciate these valuable schools; they are doing a vast amount of good to our people.

articles.headline: The "22d." / Departure of the Troops (22nd USCT through Philadelphia)
articles.summary: The 22d (Colored) Regiment is now full, and is expecting every day to leave for the "Sunny South." The 3d, 4th and 6th Colored Regiments have been in several severe engagements ... Departure of the Troops. Since the above was penned, the above named regiment has broken camp ... The regiment came into this city on last Wednesday morning, arriving at Berks Station at about 11 o'clock, and proceeded through the following streets: Down Second to Arch; up Arch to Broad; down Broad to Chestnut; down Chestnut to Third, (where they were reviewed at some length by General Meade;) down Third to Lombard; down Lombard to Second; down Second to Washington, and down Washington to the Union and Cooper Volunteer Refreshment Saloons. (Also named, reading uncertain: Sarah Holland [VERIFY] (colored young lady serving soldiers at the Union Volunteer Refreshment Saloon since it began (Miss)).)

articles.headline: Died: Alice Moore (Bethel)
articles.summary: On the 6th of January, 1864 [year VERIFY], Sister Alice Moore, aged one hundred and three years, and was interred in the old Bethel burying ground, in this city, on the 8th of Jan. Sister Moore was a member of Bethel church for many years, faithful and true. She died in the triumphs of faith.

articles.headline: Wilberforce University: An Appeal to the Conferences
articles.author: John G. Mitchell
articles.summary: The plan adopted by the Trustees to raise means to liquidate the debt of Wilberforce University was that there should be one hundred or more grand bazaars held in the different parts of the country, commencing on the evening of the 25th of December, and closing on the 1st of January ... two thousand three hundred dollars must be raised to meet the second payment ... due on the 10th of March. Signed for the Executive Committee: John G. Griffin [as read], President; Bishop D. A. Payne, D.D.; Rev. E. D. Davis; Andrew J. Holland; John G. Mitchell, Sec'y. (Ohio; only Bishop Payne linked.)

articles.headline: Obituary: Rothey Ann James (formerly of Bethel, Philadelphia)
articles.author: Henry Ha[...] [VERIFY]
articles.summary: We once more mourn over the loss of a departed friend, Sister Rothey [VERIFY] Ann James, who was born in Delaware, near Dover, on the 16th of April, 1817. When she arrived over womanhood, she removed to Philadelphia, and embraced religion in the early part of her life, and joined the A. M. E. Bethel Church, where she remained a worthy member while she lived. She was married to Mr. Eli Z. James, on the 31st of January, 1855, in Philadelphia, where they remained some three years, and then removed to Progress, N. J. ... on the 26th of January, 1864, she departed this life ... aged 47 years, 9 months and 10 days; and on the 30th of Jan. she was buried. (Also named, reading uncertain: Rothey Ann James [VERIFY] (deceased; member of Bethel, Philadelphia; died Progress, N. J., Jan. 26, 1864 (Sister)).)

articles.headline: Bethel trustee Henry Brooks answers 'An Elder censured for doing his duty' (Campbell and the Bethel trustees)
articles.author: Henry Brooks
articles.summary: I see in the Recorder of the [date illegible] of Jan. 1864, an article headed "An Elder censured for doing his duty." My desire is to give to the public a true and unvarnished statement of the case. This suit was brought for slander, and not for the illegality of charges against me by Jabez P. Campbell at a meeting on the 11th of June, 1863. It is the practice of the Trustees to make their annual report before the Election for Trustees takes place. The report of the Trustees was received by the Corporation but rejected by Jabez P. Campbell. There was then a committee of three appointed, consisting of Robert Wilson, Abraham Fields, and the Rev. Stephen Smith, to audit the accounts from 1862 until 1863 ... Signed Henry Brooks, Phila., Feb., 1864.

articles.headline: On Revivals (J. P. Campbell at Waters Chapel, Baltimore)
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: Dear Brother Weaver: For a few months, I have been a providential sojourner in the monumental City. At the earnest solicitation of the official Board of Waters Chapel, through Rt. Rev. Bishop D. A. Payne, D.D., I came here to take charge of Waters Chapel Station, and Tessier St. Mission, until the ensuing Baltimore Annual Conference ... Oct. 29th, 1863, I entered upon the duties of this charge ... the days of our most pleasant sojourn will perhaps soon be ended, when we shall have to return to our old field of labor, the Philadelphia Conference, because in coming here we did not obtain a transfer from the Philadelphia to the Baltimore Conference. Signed J. P. Campbell, Baltimore, February 13th, 1864.

articles.headline: A Soldier's Letter (3d U.S.C.T. thanks the Central Presbyterian Church)
articles.author: Henry S. Ha..ood [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Camp of the 3d U. S. C. T., January 16th, 1864. Mr. Robert T. Jones. Sir: I received a communication from you dated Dec. 22d, in which you stated that the members of the Central Presbyterian Church had made up a box of articles for our hospital use. Believe me, sir, that we feel very grateful to those who thought enough of the poor soldier who is languishing on a bed of affliction ... tell them the soldiers of the third U. S. C. T. will cherish the memory of that act of kindness ... Signed Henry S. Ha[..]ood [VERIFY], Serg't of Co. B, 3d U. S. C. T., Morris Island, S. C. (Also named, reading uncertain: Henry S. Ha..ood [VERIFY] (Sergeant, Co. B, 3d U. S. C. T., Morris Island, S. C. (signer)).)

articles.headline: Letter from New Haven (mentions Rev. L. J. Hall, formerly of the Philadelphia Conference)
articles.summary: New Haven, Ct., Feb. 15th [as read], 1864. Mr. Editor: The Christian Recorder has made its appearance once more, after an absence of two weeks ... I have held my third Quarterly Meeting ... The appointments on Sabbath were as follows: Grimes, at half past ten o'clock, Rev. Wm. H. Ross, at half past two o'clock; Rev. L. J. Hall [VERIFY], formerly of the Philadelphia Conference, but now is Capt. Norton's Orderly Sergeant of the 29th Reg. Conn. (Col. Vol.) at 7 P. M. ... (Also complains that the 29th Connecticut's flag, bought by colored citizens, was presented by a white man. Signed Wm. W. Grimes [as read, not verified].)

articles.headline: To Our Many Inquiring Friends (Mrs. Weaver's illness)
articles.summary: Many of our dear friends have written to us to know how Mrs. Weaver is. As we have not the time to write each one a single letter, we will answer each one in all. Mrs. Weaver is at death's door, and, from appearances, ere this shall have reached all of our patrons, it is thought that she will be with the angels in heaven.

articles.headline: Our Up-town Carrier / Australia (Hollowell; Daniel P. Adger)
articles.summary: Our good brother, Hollowell, who carries the Recorder up-town, is doing a good work. He is increasing his list every week. That's right brother Hollowell ... Australia. Our young and worthy friend, Mr. Daniel P. [VERIFY] Adger, has sent us several copies of the papers printed in that portion of the world, viz: Sydney, N. S. W. One is called the Herald. Many thanks. We have also the Argus published at Melbourne. (Also named, reading uncertain: Daniel P. Adger [VERIFY] ('our young and worthy friend', sent Australian newspapers (Mr.)).)

articles.headline: The Pay of Colored Soldiers (editorial)
articles.summary: We are sorry to see that the Senate of the United States Congress has refused to pay our colored soldiers the same as the white soldiers from the time they were mustered into the service of the United States; but it seems that their pay is only to commence from the first of January, 1864. We do sincerely hope that the House will do better than that ... Soldiers, cheer up, for we hope that there is a better day coming.

articles.headline: Letter from Yorktown: 'Bought and Sold', a drafted soldier of the 6th U.S.C.T., on pay and his starving family
articles.author: Bought and Sold
articles.summary: Yorktown, Va., Feb. [day illegible], 1864. Mr. Editor: I am a soldier, or at least, that is what I was drafted for, in the 6th U. S. C. T.; have been in the service since Aug., last. I could not afford to get a substitute, or I would not be here now, and my poor wife at home almost starving ... our officers tell us now, that we are not soldiers; that if we were, we would get the same pay as the white men; that the government just called us out to dig and drudge, that we are to get but $7 00 per month ... When I was at Chelton Hill I felt very patriotic; but my wife's letters have brought my patriotism down to the freezing point ... Signed Bought and Sold.

articles.headline: Died: Mrs. Catherine Bowers Rock, wife of John S. Rock of Boston (sister of Mrs. Duterte)
articles.summary: In this city, on the 6th [VERIFY] inst., of consumption, Mrs. Catherine Bowers, wife of John S. Rock, Esq., of Boston. In Mrs. Rock's experience we have a valuable lesson to all believers, and encouragement to all who will be saved by Christ's precious blood. More than two years before her death, Mrs. Rock lost her attachment for the pleasures of this life ... About fifteen months ago, she took a heavy cold ... About the 1st of December she was taken down to her bed ... Her mother (Mrs. Bowers) and her sister (Mrs. Duterte,) to whom she was very much attached, believed her to be converted ... (Her husband read to her from a little book on the Blood of Christ left by the Rev. Mr. Alleton [as printed; later 'Mr. Allstne'].)
people: deceased (printed 'Mrs. Catherine Bowers, wife of John S. Rock'); died in Philadelphia of consumption, Feb. 1864

articles.headline: Letter from Trenton: New Brunswick church under William Offer
articles.author: William Moore
articles.summary: Trenton, February 3d, 1864. Mr. Editor: It is due to the people of New Brunswick, that some one should speak a word in their behalf ... It will be remembered that under the pastoral charge of the Rev. G. W. Johnson, the people of New Brunswick unfortunately built a new church, which has remained in an unfinished condition ever since. No young pastor has ever taken charge under a more unfavorable aspect than their present pastor, brother William Offer. When he arrived there, he found the roof blown off the church ... a debt of $1200 upon it ... finished the basement at a cost of $420 ... Signed William Moore, Elder in Charge.

articles.summary: We have been informed that the sum of one hundred and forty dollars was raised in this church on last Sabbath to pay the impending dues. This is quite refreshing and speaks well for the proverbial liberality of the people of this church. They can perform wonders when so disposed.

Bishop Quinn was wont to tarry by the wayside in his journeyings to and fro, has left this world of care to sing praises at the throne on high. A true Christian, doing as she would be done by ...

articles.headline: Washington's Birthday: colored troops salute the procession before the Supervisory Committee's office (editorial)
articles.summary: The birth day of the Father of his Country was celebrated in this city with more than usual enthusiasm ... We learned from a communication in the Press of the 23d inst., that a detachment of colored United States troops were drawn up before the office of the Supervisory Committee, and with heads uncovered, saluting the procession as it passed their head quarters. Many of the officers and men, particularly the veterans ..., saluted this colored guard ... But some of the officers and men sneered at this expression of loyalty on the part of black men, and marched by in contemptuous silence, with averted faces.

articles.headline: Colored Soldiers and the Government (editorial on equal pay)
articles.summary: There are thousands of colored men at the present time who have been solicited to enlist by agents who claimed to be authorized to do so by the Government or War Department ... thousands of them have enlisted, with the promise that they would be allowed the same pay as white soldiers ... The question now is, has Congress allowed the colored soldier the same pay as the white? Has the colored soldier received it?

Father Murphy gives evidence of being a true and faithful minister of Christ. At night brother Williams, of Bethel Church, Baltimore, preached ... Signed J. P. Campbell, Baltimore, Md., Feb. 15 [as read], 1864.

articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: The discipline of the A. M. E. Church says, "The General Conference shall not do away the privileges of our ministers or preachers, of trial by a committee, and of an appeal. Bethel Church to elect three trustees, to fill the vacancy occurring at that time by the expiration of the term of Mr. Henry Brooks and others ... the minority protesting against it, denying the right of the elder to nominate trustees. articles.headline: Obituary: Rachel Growden (Attleborough, Bucks Co.)
articles.author: Charles Conover, Sr.
articles.summary: We have, mournfully, to record the death of our friend and sister, Rachel Growden, wife of Thomas Growden, who departed this life on the evening of the 23d of February, 1864, in the sixty-fifth year of her age ... Sister Growden sought religion when young, somewhere about the seventeenth year of her age, when Father Peppers used to hold the meetings in a cooper-shop in Trenton. She leaves an affectionate husband and two children. On Sabbath, the 28th ult., Father Murray and the Rev. Mr. Crispin delivered a fine sermon. Attleborough, Bucks Co., March 1, 1864.

articles.headline: Bishop Nazrey's spring appointments; Philadelphia Annual Conference to sit at Salem, N. J.
articles.author: Willis Nazrey
articles.summary: Wilkesburgh, Pa., March 18th, 1864. Mr. Editor: Please publish the following: I will be at Trenton, New Jersey, on the 29th; at Princeton on the 30th; at Brunswick on the 1st of April; at Bordentown on the 2d; at Allentown on the 4th; at Freehold on the 5th; at Riceville on the 6th and 7th; at Mana[?]lphen on the 8th; at Oxford, Pa., on the 12th; at Calvary on the 13th; at Little Britain on the 14th; at Penningtonville on the 15th; at Lancaster on the 17th; at Columbia on the 18th; and at Marietta on the 19th ... P. S. The preachers in charge will attend to their financial duties before leaving for the General Conference, as they will not have time to return to their circuits after the General Conference is over, because the Annual Conference will sit on the Saturday after the rise of the General Conference ... Salem, New Jersey, at which the Conference is to be held, is a weak point.

articles.author: A. Burris
articles.summary: To Our Kind Friends and Patrons. I have seen the very humane appeal made by the Editor of the 'Christian Recorder,' for aid to send the 'Christian Recorder' to our brave colored soldiers now upon the battle-field ... we therefore agree to give one of our interesting, amusing, and entertaining old Folks' Continental Concerts, on Thursday evening, April 21st, at the Sansom St. Hall, half of the proceeds to go towards sending the paper to our brave troops. articles.headline: One of the Monagan Family (assault on James W. Brown; refuge in a passenger car)
articles.summary: Patrick Monagan was arraigned at the Central Station, on the charge of committing an assault and battery, and, with others, mobbing and chasing James W. Brown, a respectable colored man. It seems, from the evidence, that on the 14th inst., this man and some other soldiers were standing at Tenth and Washington Streets; the witness, coming from a funeral, passed by; the whole crowd mobbed him ... he ran for safety, and the crowd gave chase, he finally took refuge in a passenger car; two of the soldiers got in, and one of them caught him by the neck; the defendant was one of the most active in the mob.

articles.headline: From Camp Shelton [Chelten] Hill, Pa. (visit to Camp William Penn)
articles.summary: Last Sabbath we accompanied the Rev. Stephen Smith to where colored men are drilled for the service of the Government of the United States. At this place hundreds of white and colored people swarm on Sundays ... there are three regiments here, the Twenty-fifth, Thirty-second and Forty-third. The Twenty-fifth is ready to strike tents ... we called upon Colonel Wagoner ... came up with the Rev. John Morgan, who, we believe, is in the Forty-third Regiment, Co. C. He left his circuit, and has gone as a soldier ... William Still, Esq., is the elected post-sutler.

events.name: Marriage of Jas. E. Moston and Henrietta Tilghman
events.description: By the Rev. W. D. W. Schureman, Mr. Jas. E. Moston [VERIFY] of Philadelphia to Miss Henrietta Tilghman of Baltimore, Md.

events.name: Death and burial of Cassella Peterson Craig
events.location: Woodbury, N.J.; burial Johnson's Cemetery, Camden
events.description: Died suddenly Dec. 23, 1863, at Woodbury, N.J.; wife of Thomas Craig; daughter of Mary Trusty [VERIFY] and the late Rev. D. H. Peterson; interred in Johnson's Cemetery, Camden, Sabbath Dec. 27, 1863. (Also named, reading uncertain: Cassella Peterson Craig [VERIFY] (deceased).)

events.name: Bethel A.M.E. Church renovation debt cleared; quarterly meeting and love-feasts announced
events.location: Bethel A.M.E. Church, S. Sixth Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Schureman reports Bethel repaired and renovated at $1600; a collection a few Sabbaths before of $727.85, a holiday fair clearing $755.81 and $200 collected by Rev. S. Smith liquidated the debt; $100 placed with the Treasurer of the Philadelphia District for Wilberforce University. Book Concern collection set for next Sabbath at 3 p.m. (Jan. 17). Bethel quarterly meeting Jan. 24, love-feast evening of Jan. 25; quarterly meeting at Zion Mission Jan. 31; love-feast Monday evening Feb. 1.

events.name: Book Concern collection at Bethel Church
events.description: Sabbath afternoon at 3 o'clock, collection for the Book Concern and the Recorder, set apart by Schureman after the Union A.M.E. trustees refused Weaver on Jan. 3.

events.name: First quarterly meeting of the West Section Mission
events.location: Hall on Lombard Street, near the S.E. corner of Broad, Philadelphia
events.description: 'Our West Section Mission': first quarterly meeting held in this section, called by Thomas H. Cooper, City Missionary, to establish the mission in this part of the city.

events.name: Quarterly meeting at Union A.M.E. Church
events.description: Announced in A. L. Stanford's N.B. Stanford protests the 'Disappointment at Union' article; Weaver's Answer states the trustees objected (1) that he had not visited and preached at Union since the present elder took charge, as he did under elder Davis, and (2) that the request was not made to them first.

events.name: Shiloh Baptist Church resolutions on Rev. Jeremiah Asher's chaplaincy
events.description: Rev. Jeremiah Asher, nearly fifteen years pastor, appointed chaplain of the 6th U.S.C.T. (Camp near Yorktown, Va.), granted twelve months' leave. Resolutions done by order of the church, December 29th [VERIFY day], 1863. Signed: Deacons Westward F. Keeling [VERIFY], John S. Kinney [VERIFY], Robert Ruffin, Spencer Mitchell, Peter Quinn [VERIFY]; Trustees James M. Auter [VERIFY], Abraham Robinson; Clerk John Brown.
attendees: pastor of Shiloh Baptist Church nearly fifteen years; appointed chaplain, 6th U.S.C.T. (Rev.)

events.description: Dec. 24, 1863: John Soare [VERIFY] and Louisa Jackson, both of Philadelphia. Dec. 31, 1863: Edward Sparrow [VERIFY] of Philadelphia and Martha Waters [VERIFY] of Trenton; same evening Joseph H. Stevens [VERIFY] and Mary E. Mitchell, both of Philadelphia.

events.name: Frankford meeting to honor seventeen enlisted colored volunteers
events.description: The evening after seventeen young men of Frankford enlisted (fifteen army, two navy), a meeting at the A.M.E. Church opened with the hymn 'Hark! Listen to the Trumpeters'; prayer by Mr. Henderson Davis, Sr.; Mr. Henderson Davis chairman; Mr. William S. Walker secretary; two or three gentlemen addressed the recruits. Enlisted: James W. Davis, Alexander Bedford, Thomas Davis, Charles Somers, Joseph Lancaster, Benjamin Jackson, Jeremiah Murray, Silas Little, Benjamin Little, Elias [VERIFY] Cary, Thomas Calvin Trusty, Edward P. Marks, James Butler, Andrew Trusty, Samuel Shorter, Benjamin Woodlin [VERIFY], Albert Farral [VERIFY]. Committee: Jacob Trusty, Peter R. Blake [VERIFY], Randall Pleasant [VERIFY]. Date not printed (January 1864). (Also named, reading uncertain: Elias Cary [VERIFY] (enlisted).)

events.name: Departure of the 8th U.S.C.T. from Camp William Penn
events.location: Chelten Hill; crossed to New Jersey from the foot of Walnut Street, Philadelphia
events.description: The 8th Regiment U.S. Colored Troops left Chelten Hill on Jan. 16, 1864, rumored bound for Hilton Head or Texas; crossed to Jersey from the foot of Walnut Street before an immense crowd, white and colored, and took the cars for New York.

events.name: Banneker Institute annual election
events.description: Officers for 1864: President, Jacob C. White, Jr.; Vice-President, John W. Simpson; Recording Secretary, William H. Dorsey [VERIFY] (signs 'Rec. Sec.'); Corresponding Secretary, Joseph Brister [VERIFY]; Treasurer, William H. Minton [VERIFY]. Committee on Debates and Lectures: John W. Simpson, chairman, Joshua B. Matthews [VERIFY], George B. White [VERIFY].
attendees: vice-president; chairman, committee on debates and lectures

events.name: Death of Joseph R. Adger
events.description: Joseph R. Adger, in his 19th year, died Jan. 22, 1864 after a short illness; served in July 1863 in the first colored company formed in the city/state for the defence of the State during the rebel raid; then sought a commission to recruit for colored regiments; shipped aboard U.S. Ship Ticonderoga; taken sick and carried to his father's on Jan. 18. Obituary signed James W. Brown. Editorial (p2) identifies the father as Mr. Adger, a large furniture dealer in South St.

events.name: Elder Schureman's quarterly meeting at Bethel; Little Wesley protracted meeting
events.location: Bethel A.M.E. Church and (Little) Wesley Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Weaver heard young Brother Berley [VERIFY] preach at Bethel (1 Samuel 12:23) at Elder Schureman's quarterly meeting, choir full. Afternoon at Wesley Church (elder Joseph Smith), sermon by Father Murray, local preacher, after a two-week protracted meeting; Brother Smith and Brother James Fuller endorsed the Recorder; seven or eight subscribed. Weaver urges 1,000 subscribers from Bethel, Wesley, Union and Zion Mission.

events.name: Henry Brooks vs. Rev. J. P. Campbell slander suit, verdict for defendant
events.description: Henry Brooks (Bethel trustee April 1860 to April 1863 and acting agent; expelled after a June 11, 1863 church trial on a tenant's complaint that her rent receipts were altered) sued Rev. Jabez P. Campbell for announcing his expulsion for fraud from the Bethel pulpit. Ex-Judge Parsons for plaintiff; William S. Pierce, Esq., for defendant. Judge Hare charged the jury that without malice there could be no recovery; verdict for Campbell, Friday morning Jan. 22, 1864. Campbell's account (dated Jan. 22) recounts the April 1863 annual report dispute, a tenant's complaint of May 2, 1863, affidavit of June 2, trial June 11, committee reports June 22 and about Aug. 11, 1863 acquitting all but the agent. Schureman's letter (Jan. 25) adds that the church exonerated the rest of the Trustee Board.

events.name: Wilberforce Committee of the Philadelphia Annual Conference meets
events.description: Committee appointed by the Philadelphia Annual Conference to receive pledges made at the last Annual Conference called to meet at 11 o'clock by Stephen Smith, chairman. Weaver's editorial notes the Wilberforce executive committee's appeal for the amount due March 10, 1864.

events.name: West End Mission preaching resumed
events.location: South-east corner of Broad and Lombard Streets, Philadelphia
events.description: A.M.E. Mission preaching every Sabbath at 10:30 a.m. and 7 p.m. (the City Missionary Thomas H. Cooper's hall per Jan. 9-23 notices).

events.name: Macedonia A.M.E. Church (South Camden) salary presentation
events.location: A.M.E. Macedonia Church, South Camden, N.J.
events.description: Three women collected $30 toward their pastor's salary, presented through the preacher's steward: Mrs. Sarah E. Brown $14.75, Mrs. Rosanna Barnes $10.00, Mrs. Emily Fisher $5.25. Pastor not named.

events.name: Death of William Carpenter
events.description: William Carpenter, in his 59th year, member of the First Colored M. P. (Israel) Church, died the morning of Jan. 18 after a lingering illness; survived by a wife (verse).

events.name: Grand Tabernacle, Independent Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity: quarterly session
events.location: new Masonic Hall, South 11th St., Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly Session of the Grand Tabernacle called for March 4, 1864, at 2 o'clock in the afternoon, the Tabernacles to make their quarterly terms. By order of James H. Smith, Grand Worthy Superior; Nathaniel Wiggins [VERIFY], Grand Recording Scribe. Notice marked 2w.

events.name: 22nd USCT marches through Philadelphia and is fed at the Union and Cooper Volunteer Refreshment Saloons
events.location: Berks Station; Second, Arch, Broad, Chestnut, Third, Lombard, Second and Washington streets; Union and Cooper Volunteer Refreshment Saloons, Philadelphia
events.description: The 22d (Colored) Regiment, raised at Camp William Penn, broke camp and came into the city 'on last Wednesday morning' (date not stated; the item was written before the issue of Feb. 13), arriving at Berks Station about 11 o'clock and marching down Second to Arch, up Arch to Broad, down Broad to Chestnut, down Chestnut to Third (reviewed at some length by General Meade), down Third to Lombard, down Lombard to Second, down Second to Washington, to the Union and Cooper Volunteer Refreshment Saloons. Headed by Colonels Wagner and Kiddoo (the latter commanding the regiment as it left). The writer condemns the jeers of bystanders. About 3 o'clock, 1,000 strong, they dined: the right wing at the Union Saloon, where 'one interesting colored young lady by the name of Miss Sarah Holland [VERIFY]' had served since the saloon first began; Union Saloon managers named: Messrs. Brown [VERIFY] (Treasurer), Wade (Sec'y) and Myers; also Mrs. A. Elkinton [VERIFY], Mrs. Wade, Miss Mary Grover, Mr. Chas. H. Greaves. At the Cooper Saloon, Mr. Cooper; ladies Mrs. E. M. Cooper, Mrs. E. Vansdale [VERIFY], Mrs. S. Ewing, Mrs. Plant, Mrs. Haines, Mrs. Deany [VERIFY], Mrs. Cowen [VERIFY], Mrs. Turner, Mrs. Mellon, Miss K. Alexander, Miss M. C. Cooper, Miss E. Whetstone and Miss C. T. Cooper (saloon volunteers, presumably white; listed here, not linked). The regiment embarked on the vessel 'Governor Chase' for Yorktown or Hilton Head. 'Mr. Carson informed us that the 25th regiment lacks but forty men of its quota.' Ends with a plea that Congress see justice done to these men.

events.name: Bethel Church (Philadelphia) corporation meeting: trustees' annual reports
events.description: Per Henry Brooks's letter (Feb. 1864): trustees' annual report received by the Corporation but rejected by Jabez P. Campbell (pastor and ex-officio President of the Trustee Board, May 1862 to April 1863); an auditing committee of three (Robert Wilson, Abraham Fields, Rev. Stephen Smith) appointed to audit the accounts from 1862 until 1863, which when called upon on the 22d of June refused to report (Stephen Smith never met the committee). Brooks was summoned by a note from Robert Wilson, signed by Campbell, to appear for trial at the study of Bethel Church on June 11, 1863, and entered his protest with six other trustees. On June 22, 1863 Brooks made his annual report of moneys received and paid over to the trustees ($106 50 [VERIFY]), receipted by Campbell; all reports were received and adopted and the Corporation exonerated him and others of embezzlement charges.
attendees: trustee of Bethel Church; reported and protested
printed 'Jabez P. Campbell'; pastor, ex-officio President of Trustees (Rev.)

events.name: Bethel Sabbath School exhibition
events.description: Exhibition by the Sabbath School connected with Bethel Church, Tuesday March 1, 1864, half-past 7 o'clock; admittance 20 cents, children under twelve 10 cents; tickets at the book store, No. 619 Pine street, and at the door. Proceeds for the school and other purposes. Superintendent Mr. L. R. Seymour; speakers 'pupils of well-known ability' (not named).

events.name: A. Burris' troupe: Great Sacred Concert
events.description: Sacred concert of vocal and instrumental music, Thursday March 3, 1864, 8 o'clock; tickets 25 cents at the principal hotels and restaurants, of any of the troupe, and at the A. M. E. Book Store, No. 619 Pine St. Programme from Haydn's Creation and Handel's Sacred Songs. Sopranos: Miss Draper, Miss Carney, Miss Livingston, Miss Williams, Miss Jenkins. Contraltos: Mrs. Bradley, Miss Hall, Miss Price, Miss Burris, Miss Jones. Tenor: Mr. Jas. B. Saunders. Basso: Mr. John Draper. Piano: Prof. Newland presiding; piano solo (Haydn's Hymn arr. Grobe) by Miss A. E. Burris; cornet accompaniment by Mr. Jacob Hoyer [VERIFY]. Trio 'On, Bright Bird' by Mrs. Bradley, Jenkins and Burris; duet by Misses Carney and Price. Conductor and Musical Director, A. Burris.

events.name: Funeral sermon of Mrs. Catherine Young
events.location: Zion Mission Church, South Seventh Street, below Dickerson, Philadelphia
events.description: Funeral sermon of Mrs. Catherine Young to be preached Sunday Feb. 28, 1864, at three o'clock, by the elder in charge, W. D. Scheroman [VERIFY spelling; = W. D. W. Schureman].

events.name: Bethel Church trustee election and the Brooks-Campbell dispute (sequence of 1863 meetings)
events.location: A. M. E. Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: As stated by J. P. Campbell (Feb. 13, 1864): April 6, 1863, annual election at Bethel to elect three trustees (terms of Mr. Henry Brooks and others expired); chairman, secretary and judges appointed; the preacher in charge (Campbell) nominated, the nominations were confirmed, the minority protesting the elder's right to nominate. Brooks preferred charges against Campbell, tried by a committee at the Annual Conference, May 18, 1863: Charge 1, nominating trustees and declaring them elected (referred to the Bishop); Charge 2, attempting to force the nominees, Peter D. Lewis [VERIFY] and Abraham Fields, at an adjourned meeting of the trustees on May 7th. Bishop W. Nazrey's decision before the Bethel corporation, May 26, 1863: the elder had the right to nominate under the 1860 General Conference enactment; a double list should be presented; male members may accept or reject; legal voters then appoint judges. Election held June 1, 1863: Campbell's double list ruled out; of 199 corporate male members fewer than 70 took part (57 counted). June 2: affidavit of Mrs. Johnson against Henry Brooks read in the official board; a steward preferred charges against several former trustees. June 11: case tried; June 22: verdict of guilty signed; same day 24 male members (of 1200 members and 199 legal voters) met and voted 24 to 0 that the accused were not guilty (meeting considered illegal by Campbell's side). About August 11, 1863: committee's final report exempted the others, found Brooks alone guilty of fraud; Brooks pronounced no longer a member at an official board meeting and a general class meeting; Brooks appealed to the Quarterly Conference and a new trial was granted. A council of elders (resolutions printed Sept. 19, 1863) found no cause of action against Campbell, who then resigned 'for the sake of peace' and went to Baltimore; Brooks thereafter sued him. Campbell notes he was a son of Bethel 'of more than thirty years' standing', sent into the ministry twenty-five years ago.

events.name: Baltimore meeting on colored enlistment, Sharp Street Church
events.location: Sharp Street Church (M. E.), Baltimore, Md.
events.description: Reported by J. P. Campbell (Baltimore Correspondence, dated March 9, 1864). First of a series of public meetings of colored men of Maryland on the causes of slow Black enlistment. Judge Bond presided; addressed by Hon. Judge Bond, Hon. Mr. Mathews (late of the State Legislature), Rev. J. Bowser [VERIFY spelling] and Rev. J. P. Campbell. The letter states the colored men of Maryland want equal pay, equal bounty, equal pensions, equal rights and equal suffrage, and that unequal remuneration has hindered enlistment; four meetings held in the past week, another series planned. Out of town: only Campbell (AME clergy) linked.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference (A. M. E.) 1864 -- announced to sit at Salem, N. J.
events.description: Bishop Willis Nazrey's notice (dated Wilkesburgh, Pa., March 18, 1864) announces that the Philadelphia Annual Conference will sit at Salem, N. J., on the Saturday after the rise of the General Conference (held in Philadelphia, May 1864); preachers in charge are to settle their financial duties before leaving for the General Conference. Also lists Nazrey's visitation of the N. J. and Pennsylvania circuits, March 29 to April 19, 1864 (Trenton, Princeton, Brunswick, Bordentown, Allentown, Freehold, Riceville, Oxford, Calvary, Little Britain, Penningtonville, Lancaster, Columbia, Marietta). Date not yet fixed in the notice.

events.name: Union A. M. E. Church fair and Prof. A. Burris's Grand Soiree
events.location: Union A. M. E. Church, Coates Street between Fourth and Fifth, Philadelphia
events.description: Church fair for the benefit of Union A. M. E. Church, opening Monday evening, March 28, 1864, and continuing the week, with useful and fancy articles and refreshments; Professor A. Burris to give a Grand Soiree in the church on Friday evening (printed 'the 2d of April'; Friday was April 1, 1864) at 7:30. Officers: Mrs. Sarah Davis, President; Mrs. Maria T. Hallowell, Secretary.

events.name: Ladies' Union Association fair at Concert Hall
events.description: Week-long fair of the Ladies' Union Association (a Black women's soldiers' relief association), opening March 28, 1864, at Concert Hall; season tickets 25 cents, sold at the Book Store, 619 Pine Street. No officers named in this notice.

events.name: Mob assault on James W. Brown at Tenth and Washington Streets
events.location: Tenth and Washington Streets, Philadelphia; Central Station (hearing)
events.description: James W. Brown, 'a respectable colored man' returning from a funeral, was mobbed and chased by a crowd of (white) soldiers at Tenth and Washington Streets on March 14, 1864; he took refuge in a city passenger car, where two soldiers followed and one seized him by the neck. Patrick Monagan was arraigned at the Central Station for assault and battery and held; the Recorder approves.

events.name: Editor's and Rev. Stephen Smith's visit and service at Camp William Penn
events.location: Camp William Penn, Chelten Hills (printed 'Camp Shelton Hill'), Pa.
events.description: On Sunday, March 20, 1864 (the 'last Sabbath' before the Mar 26 issue), the editor (E. Weaver) and Rev. Stephen Smith visited Camp William Penn, where the 25th, 32nd and 43rd USCT were in camp (the 25th ready to leave). Received by Colonel Wagoner [Wagner, the white commandant]; met Rev. John Morgan, who had left his circuit to enlist, believed in the 43rd Regiment, Co. C; afternoon service at 3:30: Smith preached on 'Put ye on the whole armour'; the editor spoke; a young licensed preacher Mr. Miller had been recommended to Col. Wagoner as chaplain, which the editor thought unsuitable. The editor complains of the disposition to put white men in every honorable place over colored troops and hopes Pennsylvania will secure colored chaplains, saying the prejudice is believed to lie with the Supervisory Committee, Colonel Wagoner and his men. William Still, Esq., the elected post sutler, and his brother were met; the sutler's store is closed on the Lord's day.
